question: What is the main message or lesson that the poet wants us to learn from the poem 'Try Again'? 🌟
options: To give up when things get hard 😔
To keep trying until we succeed 🏆
To ask someone else to do our work 🤝
To rest and forget our goals 😴
answer: To keep trying until we succeed 🏆
explanation: Awesome! The poem beautifully teaches us that failure is just a stepping stone, and we must never lose hope and always try again!
hint: The title of the poem gives away the biggest clue.

question: According to the poem, what should you do if at first you don't succeed? 🤔
explanation: Brilliant! The poet emphasizes that the immediate response to not succeeding the first time is to try again with more effort.
hint: It is the main repeating phrase in the poem.

question: What does the word 'heed' mean in the line 'Tis a lesson you should heed'? 📖
explanation: Excellent! 'Heed' means to listen to advice or pay close attention to an important lesson.
hint: When your teacher gives you advice, you should do this.

question: What quality will appear when you decide to try again instead of giving up? 🦁
explanation: Fantastic! Facing failure and deciding to try again builds true courage in our hearts.
hint: It is the quality of being brave.

question: What does it mean to 'persevere' in the poem? 🏃‍♂️
explanation: Great job! Perseverance means never giving up, even when a task is very tough or takes a long time.
hint: It means to keep going no matter what.

question: According to the poet, what happens if you persevere? ⛰️
explanation: Super! The poet promises that if we persevere, we will eventually overcome our fears and conquer our challenges.
hint: You will win and overcome your obstacles.

question: What does the poet say about failing 'once or twice'? ✌️
options: It means you are not smart 🧠
It is the end of the world 🌍
It is normal, just try again 🌱
answer: It is normal, just try again 🌱
explanation: Awesome! Failing once or twice is a completely normal part of learning. We just need to try again!
hint: The poet uses this to show that early failures shouldn't stop us.

question: What does the word 'prevail' mean in the poem? 🌅
explanation: Brilliant! To prevail means to be victorious and achieve your goal after struggling.
hint: It means to conquer or emerge as the winner.

question: The poet says, 'If we strive, 'tis no disgrace'. What does 'strive' mean? 💦
options: To make a great effort or work hard 🏋️‍♂️
answer: To make a great effort or work hard 🏋️‍♂️
explanation: Excellent! Striving means putting in your best effort and working very hard to achieve something.
hint: It is similar to struggling or trying your absolute best.

question: Why is it 'no disgrace' if we do not win the race? 🏁
options: Because making a sincere effort is what truly matters 🏅
Because the race was too short ⏱️
answer: Because making a sincere effort is what truly matters 🏅
explanation: Fantastic! There is no shame in losing as long as you tried your hardest. The effort itself is a victory!
hint: It is not about the trophy, but the hard work you put in.

question: What should you do in case you try hard but do not win? 🛡️
explanation: Great job! Even if we don't win after striving, the only correct response is to keep trying.
hint: It is the central advice of the whole poem.

question: What does the poet tell us to do if we find our task is 'hard'? 🧱
options: Ask the teacher to cancel it 👩‍🏫
explanation: Super! Hard tasks build strong minds. When a task is difficult, we shouldn't quit, we should try again.
hint: The advice remains the same no matter the difficulty.

question: According to the poem, what will 'time' bring you if you keep trying? 🎁
explanation: Awesome! Patience and time, combined with hard work, will eventually bring you the reward of success.
hint: It is a positive outcome for all your hard work.

question: Who does the poet refer to with the word 'folks'? 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
explanation: Brilliant! 'Folks' is a friendly word used to refer to other people around us in society.
hint: It means the general public or other humans.

question: What question does the poet ask about 'other folks'? ❓
options: Why, with patience, should not you do what they can do? 🌟
Why do they sleep so much? 💤
answer: Why, with patience, should not you do what they can do? 🌟
explanation: Excellent! The poet reminds us that if other regular people can achieve great things, so can we, as long as we are patient.
hint: It is a question meant to inspire confidence in your own abilities.

question: What is the ONE rule the poet wants us to keep in view? 👀
explanation: Fantastic! The ultimate golden rule of the poem is simply to keep trying again and again.
hint: It is the title of the poem.

question: Which poetic device is used when the poet repeats the line 'Try, try again' throughout the poem? 🎵
explanation: Great job! Repeating a line or phrase in a poem is called repetition or a refrain, and it helps emphasize the main message.
hint: It means doing or saying something over and over.

question: Which quality is highlighted as necessary when looking at what other folks can do? 🧘‍♂️
explanation: Super! Patience is key. We shouldn't rush or get jealous; with patience and effort, we can achieve our goals too.
hint: It is the ability to wait calmly without getting upset.

question: What is the antonym (opposite) of the word 'succeed'? 📉
explanation: Awesome! The opposite of succeeding is failing, but the poem teaches us that failing is just a step towards success!
hint: It is what happens when you do not pass a test.

question: What is the synonym (similar meaning) of the word 'conquer'? ⚔️
explanation: Brilliant! To conquer means to overcome an obstacle or defeat a challenge successfully.
hint: Knights used to do this to dragons in stories.

question: What does the word 'disgrace' mean in the context of the poem? 😳
options: A reason to feel shame or loss of respect 😞
answer: A reason to feel shame or loss of respect 😞
explanation: Excellent! Disgrace means shame. The poet says failing after trying hard is NOT a disgrace.
hint: It is a feeling of embarrassment or shame.

question: How does the tone of the poem feel? 🌈
explanation: Fantastic! The tone is highly encouraging, pushing the reader to be positive and resilient in life.
hint: How do you feel when a coach cheers you on?

question: Which of these rhyming pairs can be found in the poem? 🎶
explanation: Great job! 'Fail' and 'prevail' end with the same sound, creating a beautiful rhyme in the second stanza.
hint: Look for the two words that sound exactly alike at the end.

question: According to the poem, should you be afraid of failure? 😨
options: Only if it is a hard task 🧱
explanation: Super! The poet tells us 'never fear', because if we persevere, we will eventually conquer our challenges.
hint: The poem tells us to be courageous.

question: What is the best alternative title for this poem? 💡
explanation: Awesome! 'Never Give Up' perfectly captures the core message of persevering and trying again.
hint: It is a popular motivational phrase about resilience.

question: If you fail a difficult math test, what does the poem advise you to do? 📝
options: Study harder and try, try again 📚
answer: Study harder and try, try again 📚
explanation: Brilliant! The poem's message applies to real life: learn from your mistakes, study hard, and try again!
hint: Apply the 'rule' mentioned in the poem to your schoolwork.

question: What does the poet mean by 'If you would at last prevail'? 🏔️
options: If you want to win in the end 🏆
If you want to go home early 🏠
If you want to give up easily 🏳️
If you want to skip the race 🚶‍♂️
answer: If you want to win in the end 🏆
explanation: Excellent! 'At last prevail' means achieving final victory after going through multiple challenges.
hint: It is about the final outcome of all your hard work.

question: Which of these words is a synonym for 'reward' as used in the poem? 🎁
explanation: Fantastic! A reward is a positive prize or benefit you receive for your patience and hard work.
hint: It is something nice you get for doing a good job.

question: Why might a task seem 'hard' at first? 🧗‍♀️
options: Because you are still learning how to do it 🧠
Because it is a bad task 👎
answer: Because you are still learning how to do it 🧠
explanation: Great job! Things often seem hard when they are new. With practice and by trying again, we learn and they become easier.
hint: Think about the first time you tried to ride a bicycle.

question: What is the poet's attitude towards making mistakes? ✏️
options: He is very angry about them 😡
He thinks they are a normal part of success 🌱
He thinks we should hide them 🫣
He thinks mistakes mean we are silly 🤡
answer: He thinks they are a normal part of success 🌱
explanation: Super! The poet understands that mistakes and failures ('once or twice') happen to everyone on the road to success.
hint: Does he tell you to quit when you fail, or keep going?

question: What does 'Time will bring you your reward' suggest about success? ⏳
options: It requires patience and does not happen overnight 🕰️
It is based purely on luck 🍀
It only happens to older people 👴
answer: It requires patience and does not happen overnight 🕰️
explanation: Awesome! True success takes time. We must be patient and keep working hard until we achieve our reward.
hint: Think about why you have to wait for a plant to grow.

question: Which word from the poem rhymes with 'race'? 🏃‍♀️
explanation: Brilliant! 'Race' and 'Disgrace' form a rhyming pair in the second stanza of the poem.
hint: Look for the word in the poem that means shame.

question: Which word from the poem rhymes with 'hard'? 🧱
explanation: Excellent! The words 'hard' and 'reward' are paired together to show that difficult work pays off.
hint: It is the prize you get for doing something well.

question: True or False: The poet believes that some tasks are just too hard and we should quit them. 🤔
options: True, ask an adult to do it 🙋‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! The poet never advises us to quit. If a task is hard, his only advice is to try, try again!
hint: What is the main message of the poem?

question: What does the phrase 'keep this rule in view' mean? 👓
options: To write the rule on a board 🖍️
To always remember and follow this principle 🧠
answer: To always remember and follow this principle 🧠
explanation: Great job! To 'keep in view' means to keep the rule in your mind and apply it in your daily life.
hint: It means to remember something important.

question: When you are learning to play a new sport and keep missing the ball, what should you do? ⚽
options: Remember the poem and try again 🔁
answer: Remember the poem and try again 🔁
explanation: Super! Missing the ball is just failing 'once or twice'. The best response is to practice and try again!
hint: Apply the rule from the poem.

question: Which of these is NOT a quality promoted by the poem? ❌
explanation: Awesome! Arrogance (being too proud) is not in the poem. The poem promotes positive traits like patience, courage, and perseverance.
hint: Look for the negative quality in the list.

question: What is the antonym of the word 'courage'? 🦁
explanation: Brilliant! Courage is being brave, so its exact opposite is cowardice or giving in to fear.
hint: It is the feeling that makes you want to run away from a challenge.

question: In the phrase 'If we strive, 'tis no disgrace', what does ''tis' stand for? ✍️
explanation: Excellent! ''Tis' is an old-fashioned poetic contraction for the words 'It is'.
hint: It is a short way of saying two very common words.

question: Who is the speaker in the poem talking to? 🗣️
explanation: Fantastic! The poet is addressing 'you', meaning all the readers, giving us universal advice for life.
hint: Who is being told to 'heed' the lesson?

question: What does the poem suggest about the relationship between patience and success? 🌱
options: They have nothing to do with each other 🤷‍♂️
Patience is a key ingredient to achieving success 🗝️
answer: Patience is a key ingredient to achieving success 🗝️
explanation: Great job! The poem explicitly links patience to achieving rewards and doing what other folks can do.
hint: Think about the line 'Why, with patience, should not you?'

question: What kind of poem is 'Try Again'? 📜
explanation: Super! A didactic poem is one that is specifically written to teach a moral lesson or give advice, just like this one!
hint: It is meant to teach you a 'lesson you should heed'.

question: If your friend fails a drawing competition and feels sad, what lines from the poem would you say to them? 🎨
options: Time will bring you your reward 🎁
explanation: Awesome! All these lines are perfect for encouraging a friend who is feeling down after a failure.
hint: Look closely, are all these options helpful and from the poem?

question: What is the rhyme scheme of the first four lines: 'heed' (A), 'again' (B), 'succeed' (A), 'again' (B)? 🎵
explanation: Brilliant! The first line rhymes with the third (A), and the second line rhymes with the fourth (B), creating an ABAB pattern.
hint: Check the ending sounds: heed (A), again (B), succeed (A), again (B).

question: Which of these is a synonym for 'task'? 📋
explanation: Excellent! A task is a piece of work, a job, or an assignment that you need to complete.
hint: It is something your teacher might give you to do.

question: How does the poet view 'other folks'? 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
options: As normal people whose successes we can match with patience 🧗‍♂️
answer: As normal people whose successes we can match with patience 🧗‍♂️
explanation: Fantastic! The poet points out that other folks are just human. If they can achieve things, we can too!
hint: He asks why you shouldn't be able to do what they do.

question: What does the poet mean by 'If you will persevere, you will conquer'? 🏔️
options: If you fight with swords, you will win a castle 🏰
If you keep trying hard, you will eventually succeed 🌟
If you sleep enough, you will wake up strong 💪
If you wait, someone else will do it ⏱️
answer: If you keep trying hard, you will eventually succeed 🌟
explanation: Great job! This is a metaphor. Conquering here means overcoming your personal challenges through hard work.
hint: It is about overcoming life's obstacles, not a literal war.

question: Which action shows a person 'heeding' the lesson of the poem? 👀
options: Giving up after losing a spelling bee 🐝
Refusing to learn how to swim because the water is cold 🏊‍♂️
Practicing the piano every day after failing an exam 🎹
Watching TV instead of doing homework 📺
answer: Practicing the piano every day after failing an exam 🎹
explanation: Super! Practicing after failing is the exact definition of 'try, try again'. This person is truly heeding the lesson!
hint: Look for the option where someone keeps trying after a setback.

question: What makes failure a 'disgrace' in real life, according to the poem's logic? 🤔
options: Quitting and not striving or trying at all 🛑
Making a mistake on a quiz 📝
answer: Quitting and not striving or trying at all 🛑
explanation: Awesome! The poem says if we strive, it is NO disgrace. Therefore, the only real disgrace is giving up without trying.
hint: Think about what is the opposite of 'striving'.

question: What is the ultimate 'reward' the poem promises? 🏆
options: Success and personal growth after hard work 🌱
answer: Success and personal growth after hard work 🌱
explanation: Brilliant! The reward isn't just a physical prize; it is the feeling of success, growth, and conquering your challenges! 🏆
hint: It is a feeling of achievement.
